articles.title: In Rajasthan, the girls who refuse to be spoken for
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: 1. Core Context & Background: Rajasthan ranks sixth among India’s States with the highest prevalence of child marriage, according to the latest National Family Health Survey (2023-24). Poverty, the lack of education, and entrenched customs such as atta-satta, reinforced by a skewed sex ratio, continue to fuel the practice, particularly in tribal and rural areas. Now, a growing number of girls, empowered by education and greater access to social media, are saying no, reports Ashok Kumar. Meanwhile, the United Nations has declared November 27 as the International Day for the Elimination of Child, Early and Forced Marriage

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: Nandini (name changed), 16, who lives in Rajasthan’s Sikar, had mapped out her future: finish school, go to college, and get a job to be financially independent. Her family, however, had other plans. Last month, they fixed her wedding without her consent. But the Class 12 student refused to surrender her dreams. She picked up her father’s mobile phone and called the 24x7 child helpline, 1098. Over the next few days, Nandini called the helpline more than six times, using whatever phone she could lay her hands on. Sometimes, she pretended she wanted to speak to her prospective groom; at other times, she sought to contact her friends. But each call carried an urgent message: wedding preparations were under way, guests were being invited, and the date was drawing closer. Help! Each time, the call was connecting to the District Child Protection Office. “She had asked us not to contact her. She said she would call whenever she got a chance. Her first call came just three days before the wedding,” recalls Gargi Sharma, District Child Protection Officer. With barely 72 hours to act, the team secured an injunction order from the court and stopped the wedding. The family was taken by surprise when officials arrived, suspecting that a neighbour had tipped them off. They never imagined that the quiet schoolgirl in their midst had been orchestrating her own rescue. Her identity as the whistleblower remained a secret.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: The Sikar administration prevented 29 child marriages in 2024 and 10 in 2025. “In 2026, we have received information about 21 cases so far,” Sharma says. But there are many Nandinis, especially in India’s villages, who do not have the education or the agency to say no to child marriage.

🏛️ Political, National & Polity Paragraph #8 of 30 (27 NOV)

📰 In Rajasthan, the girls who refuse to be spoken for

📌 Published: 27 Nov 2026, 02:45:13 AM
🎙️ Desi Hinglish Voice Educator • 🚂 Live Train Line Highlight & Screen Lock

1. Core Context & Background: Rajasthan ranks sixth among India’s States with the highest prevalence of child marriage, according to the latest National Family Health Survey (2023-24). Poverty, the lack of education, and entrenched customs such as atta-satta, reinforced by a skewed sex ratio, continue to fuel the practice, particularly in tribal and rural areas. Now, a growing number of girls, empowered by education and greater access to social media, are saying no, reports Ashok Kumar. Meanwhile, the United Nations has declared November 27 as the International Day for the Elimination of Child, Early and Forced Marriage

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: Nandini (name changed), 16, who lives in Rajasthan’s Sikar, had mapped out her future: finish school, go to college, and get a job to be financially independent. Her family, however, had other plans. Last month, they fixed her wedding without her consent. But the Class 12 student refused to surrender her dreams. She picked up her father’s mobile phone and called the 24x7 child helpline, 1098. Over the next few days, Nandini called the helpline more than six times, using whatever phone she could lay her hands on. Sometimes, she pretended she wanted to speak to her prospective groom; at other times, she sought to contact her friends. But each call carried an urgent message: wedding preparations were under way, guests were being invited, and the date was drawing closer. Help! Each time, the call was connecting to the District Child Protection Office. “She had asked us not to contact her. She said she would call whenever she got a chance. Her first call came just three days before the wedding,” recalls Gargi Sharma, District Child Protection Officer. With barely 72 hours to act, the team secured an injunction order from the court and stopped the wedding. The family was taken by surprise when officials arrived, suspecting that a neighbour had tipped them off. They never imagined that the quiet schoolgirl in their midst had been orchestrating her own rescue. Her identity as the whistleblower remained a secret.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: The Sikar administration prevented 29 child marriages in 2024 and 10 in 2025. “In 2026, we have received information about 21 cases so far,” Sharma says. But there are many Nandinis, especially in India’s villages, who do not have the education or the agency to say no to child marriage.

📚 TOP 4 HARD VOCABULARY WORDS EXTRACTED FROM THIS PARAGRAPH (TAP CARD FOR PICTURE & SYNONYMS):
Administration (Noun)
प्रशासन — इस अनुच्छेद में 'Administration' का प्रयोग एक महत्वपूर्ण प्रशासनिक और विश्लेषणात्मक अर्थ में किया गया है।
✓ Syn: Significant, Substantial, Strategic  |  ✖ Ant: Insignificant, Negligible, Trivial
International (Adjective)
अंतरराष्ट्रीय — इस अनुच्छेद में 'International' का प्रयोग एक महत्वपूर्ण प्रशासनिक और विश्लेषणात्मक अर्थ में किया गया है।
✓ Syn: Comprehensive, Influential, Decisive  |  ✖ Ant: Superficial, Ineffective, Fragile
Elimination (Noun)
उन्मूलन — इस अनुच्छेद में 'Elimination' का प्रयोग एक महत्वपूर्ण प्रशासनिक और विश्लेषणात्मक अर्थ में किया गया है।
✓ Syn: Significant, Substantial, Strategic  |  ✖ Ant: Insignificant, Negligible, Trivial
Prospective (Adjective)
भावी — इस अनुच्छेद में 'Prospective' का प्रयोग एक महत्वपूर्ण प्रशासनिक और विश्लेषणात्मक अर्थ में किया गया है।
✓ Syn: Comprehensive, Influential, Decisive  |  ✖ Ant: Superficial, Ineffective, Fragile
🧠 2 ANALYTICAL EXAM QUESTIONS BASED ON THIS EDITORIAL:
Q1. Based on a critical reading of the above 🏛️ Political, National & Polity passage on "In Rajasthan, the girls who refuse to be spoken for", which of the following statements accurately reflects the central analytical observation of the text?
A. Rajasthan ranks sixth among India’s States with the highest prevalence of child marriage, according to the latest National Family Health Survey...
B. Contrary to the passage, the issue of 'In Rajasthan, the girls who refuse to be spoken ' requires zero institutional or regulatory intervention at any level.
C. The passage argues that all empirical data and statutory mechanisms related to 'In Rajasthan, the girls who refuse to be spok' should be permanently discontinued.
D. The author contends that 'In Rajasthan, the girls who refuse to be spok' has no bearing on public governance, economy, or citizen welfare.
✅ Correct Answer: Option (A) — Sahi Jawab Option (A) hai. Is passage ki mukhya line saaf batati hai: "Rajasthan ranks sixth among India’s States with the highest prevalence of child marriage, according to the latest National Family Health Survey..." (Hinglish Arth: नवीनतम राष्ट्रीय परिवार स्वास्थ्य सर्वेक्षण (2023-24) के अनुसार, बाल विवाह के सबसे अधिक प्रसार वाले भारत के राज्यों में राजस्थान छठे स्थान पर है।)
Q2. Which of the following key analytical points or conclusions is explicitly highlighted by the author in the passage regarding "In Rajasthan, the girls who refuse to be spoken for"?
A. Advocating complete policy paralysis and ignoring ground-level implementation challenges.
B. But there are many Nandinis, especially in India’s villages, who do not have the education or the agency to say no to child marriage.
C. Dismissing constitutional accountability and relying solely on unverified short-term measures.
D. Recommending the immediate suspension of all regulatory and scientific assessments mentioned in the text.
✅ Correct Answer: Option (B) — Sahi Jawab Option (B) hai. Lekhak ne passage ke vishleshan mein is baat par zor diya hai: "But there are many Nandinis, especially in India’s villages, who do not have the education or the agency to say no to child marriage." (Hinglish Arth: लेकिन कई नंदिनी हैं, खासकर भारत के गांवों में, जिनके पास बाल विवाह को न कहने की शिक्षा या एजेंसी नहीं है।)

fullParagraphs: 1. Core Context & Background: Artificial Intelligence (AI) may transform the way Arabic is learned and used, but human emotions and traditional values remain beyond the reach of technology, an international conference on the Arabic language held at Anvarul Islam Arabic College, Kuniyil, observed on Thursday.

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: The two-day conference, titled ‘Digital humanities: reimagining Arabic language and literature’, was organised by the Arabic department of the college in association with Calicut University’s Arabic department, Kerala State Higher Education Council, and Arab Union of Internet Writers. Liyaqat Ali, deputy director of collegiate education, inaugurated the conference on Wednesday. College Principal K. Mohammed Fawaz presided over the function. Liyaqat Ali, deputy director of collegiate education, inaugurating an international conference on Arabic at Anvarul Islam Arabic College, Kuniyil, on Wednesday. | Photo Credit: SAKEER HUSSAIN Arabic scholars Sumayya Ibrahim Abu Thailath from Palestine, Najeeb Ali Mulkhath from Yemen, Simi K. Salim, K. Ali Noufal, I.P. Abdul Salam, C.M. Sabir Navas, K.A. Nasser, P. Firoz, M.K. Ameer Swalahi, Shakir Babu Kuniyil, and K.P. Abdul Haleem Thangal spoke. E.T. Mohammed Basheer, MP, inaugurated the valedictory function on Thursday. He highlighted the growing global significance of the Arabic language in an increasingly interconnected world.
3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: Scholars Mujeeb Nellikkuth, Ali Jafar, Mohammed Aman K., P. Sulaiman and C. Abdul Wahab spoke.

Contrary to the passage, the issue of 'Cultural values of language remain irreplaceable' requires zero institutional or regulatory intervention at any level.

🏛️ Political, National & Polity Paragraph #9 of 30 (27 NOV)

📰 Cultural values of language remain irreplaceable in AI era: Arabic meet

📌 Published: 27 Nov 2026, 02:24:15 AM
🎙️ Desi Hinglish Voice Educator • 🚂 Live Train Line Highlight & Screen Lock

1. Core Context & Background: Artificial Intelligence (AI) may transform the way Arabic is learned and used, but human emotions and traditional values remain beyond the reach of technology, an international conference on the Arabic language held at Anvarul Islam Arabic College, Kuniyil, observed on Thursday.

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: The two-day conference, titled ‘Digital humanities: reimagining Arabic language and literature’, was organised by the Arabic department of the college in association with Calicut University’s Arabic department, Kerala State Higher Education Council, and Arab Union of Internet Writers. Liyaqat Ali, deputy director of collegiate education, inaugurated the conference on Wednesday. College Principal K. Mohammed Fawaz presided over the function. Liyaqat Ali, deputy director of collegiate education, inaugurating an international conference on Arabic at Anvarul Islam Arabic College, Kuniyil, on Wednesday. | Photo Credit: SAKEER HUSSAIN Arabic scholars Sumayya Ibrahim Abu Thailath from Palestine, Najeeb Ali Mulkhath from Yemen, Simi K. Salim, K. Ali Noufal, I.P. Abdul Salam, C.M. Sabir Navas, K.A. Nasser, P. Firoz, M.K. Ameer Swalahi, Shakir Babu Kuniyil, and K.P. Abdul Haleem Thangal spoke. E.T. Mohammed Basheer, MP, inaugurated the valedictory function on Thursday. He highlighted the growing global significance of the Arabic language in an increasingly interconnected world.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: Scholars Mujeeb Nellikkuth, Ali Jafar, Mohammed Aman K., P. Sulaiman and C. Abdul Wahab spoke.

अंतरराष्ट्रीय — इस अनुच्छेद में 'International' का प्रयोग एक महत्वपूर्ण प्रशासनिक और विश्लेषणात्मक अर्थ में किया गया है।

महत्व — इस अनुच्छेद में 'Significance' का प्रयोग एक महत्वपूर्ण प्रशासनिक और विश्लेषणात्मक अर्थ में किया गया है।
✓ Syn: Significant, Substantial, Strategic  |  ✖ Ant: Insignificant, Negligible, Trivial
Traditional (Adjective)
परंपरागत — इस अनुच्छेद में 'Traditional' का प्रयोग एक महत्वपूर्ण प्रशासनिक और विश्लेषणात्मक अर्थ में किया गया है।

articles.title: BDO issues residence certificate to mother of child denied birth certificate due to SIR row
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: 1. Core Context & Background: Amina Khatun and Abdul Habib were denied a residence proof necessary for birth certificate on grounds that Abdul Habib’s name was struck off electoral rolls during SIR.

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: The district administration of Coochbehar district in West Bengal on Thursday (November 26, 2026) issued a residence certificate to the mother of a two-month-old infant, after her parents faced challenges to get the certificate on the ground that the name of the father was deleted from electoral rolls during the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) held earlier this year. The Hindu reported on November 25 that the birth certificate was denied to the infant because the father's name was deleted from the electoral roll during SIR. Amina Khatun, wife of Abdul Habib, gave birth to a girl at Dinhata Sub-Divisional Hospital on September 9. Amina Khatun and Abdul Habib approached the hospital and the concerned panchayat office to obtain their daughter’s birth certificate. The couple was reportedly asked to arrange residential verification from the local panchayat pradhan or MLA. On the grounds that the name of Abdul Habib was deleted from the electoral roll in the SIR, the local BJP MLA office refused to give them residence proof. On Thursday (November 26), the BDO office issued a residence certificate to Amina Khatun. “This is to certify that Amina Khatun, wife of Abdul Habib, is a permanent resident of village Khatamari P.O. Khatamari as per the enquiry report of Chowdhurihat Gram Panchayat -. Under Dinhata-II Development Block, P.S.: Sahebganj, Dist.: Cooch Behar. The name of the applicant has been enrolled in the Electoral Roll vide Part-191, Sl. No .848 of 7 Dinhata Assembly Constituency. I wish him/her all success in his/her life,” read the certificate issued by the BDO on Thursday. Abdul Hamid told this correspondent that government officials came to his residence and took him to the BDO office where the residence proof was given to him. “I have received my residence verification certificate which I am going to submit at the hospital tomorrow. Hopefully, my daughter will now get the birth certificate soon,” the father said. There have been allegations of denial of services by the West Bengal government to citizens whose names have been deleted from the electoral rolls during SIR. The Supreme Court, which oversaw the SIR process in the State, had made it clear that removal of a name from the electoral roll cannot be grounds for denial of services. The names of about 36 lakh electors deleted during SIR are pending before SIR tribunals in the State.
3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: Special Intensive Revision of electoral rolls / Election Commission of India / government

🏛️ Political, National & Polity Paragraph #10 of 30 (27 NOV)

📰 BDO issues residence certificate to mother of child denied birth certificate due to SIR row

📌 Published: 27 Nov 2026, 02:23:07 AM
🎙️ Desi Hinglish Voice Educator • 🚂 Live Train Line Highlight & Screen Lock

1. Core Context & Background: Amina Khatun and Abdul Habib were denied a residence proof necessary for birth certificate on grounds that Abdul Habib’s name was struck off electoral rolls during SIR.

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: The district administration of Coochbehar district in West Bengal on Thursday (November 26, 2026) issued a residence certificate to the mother of a two-month-old infant, after her parents faced challenges to get the certificate on the ground that the name of the father was deleted from electoral rolls during the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) held earlier this year. The Hindu reported on November 25 that the birth certificate was denied to the infant because the father's name was deleted from the electoral roll during SIR. Amina Khatun, wife of Abdul Habib, gave birth to a girl at Dinhata Sub-Divisional Hospital on September 9. Amina Khatun and Abdul Habib approached the hospital and the concerned panchayat office to obtain their daughter’s birth certificate. The couple was reportedly asked to arrange residential verification from the local panchayat pradhan or MLA. On the grounds that the name of Abdul Habib was deleted from the electoral roll in the SIR, the local BJP MLA office refused to give them residence proof. On Thursday (November 26), the BDO office issued a residence certificate to Amina Khatun. “This is to certify that Amina Khatun, wife of Abdul Habib, is a permanent resident of village Khatamari P.O. Khatamari as per the enquiry report of Chowdhurihat Gram Panchayat -. Under Dinhata-II Development Block, P.S.: Sahebganj, Dist.: Cooch Behar. The name of the applicant has been enrolled in the Electoral Roll vide Part-191, Sl. No .848 of 7 Dinhata Assembly Constituency. I wish him/her all success in his/her life,” read the certificate issued by the BDO on Thursday. Abdul Hamid told this correspondent that government officials came to his residence and took him to the BDO office where the residence proof was given to him. “I have received my residence verification certificate which I am going to submit at the hospital tomorrow. Hopefully, my daughter will now get the birth certificate soon,” the father said. There have been allegations of denial of services by the West Bengal government to citizens whose names have been deleted from the electoral rolls during SIR. The Supreme Court, which oversaw the SIR process in the State, had made it clear that removal of a name from the electoral roll cannot be grounds for denial of services. The names of about 36 lakh electors deleted during SIR are pending before SIR tribunals in the State.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: Special Intensive Revision of electoral rolls / Election Commission of India / government

articles.title: Jammu and Kashmir’s selection board’s official X handle ‘suspended’ amid anti-board protests over cheating case
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: 1. Core Context & Background: Official sources said the official handle of the Board on X was suspended on November 25, 2026, apparently due to large-scale reporting by protesting netizens online

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: The official X handle of the J&K Service Selection Board (JKSSB) was reportedly suspended on Thursday (November 26, 2026), as protests against the recruitment board continued in the wake of the recent case of cheating during the Finance Accounts Assistant (FAA) examination in Jammu. Meanwhile, activists and aspirants, who were seeking postponement of the Sub-Inspector examination, were allegedly detained in Jammu. Official sources said the official handle of the Board on X was suspended on Wednesday (November 25), apparently due to large-scale reporting by protesting netizens online. The JKSSB has not issued any statement on the suspension of its X handle. It had around 129.1K followers. Meanwhile, several aspirants held protests in Jammu against the Board and demanded postponement of the upcoming Police Sub-Inspector (PSI) examination scheduled for November 29. Meanwhile, the Board said it put in place fresh measures to check cheating. It has asked the Deputy Commissioners to appoint invigilation staff through a randomisation process, drawing from a pool of staff already identified. “Exam centres will be allotted to candidates at random, but admit cards will now be available for download only three days before the exam instead of seven,” it said. The magistrates have been tasked to supervise the frisking of candidates and exam staff. All staff deployed at a centre, including service providers, will have to hand in their mobile phones and other gadgets, which will be kept locked in the centre’s control room until the exam ends, it added. The Board also increased jammers at exam centres and pressed CCTV for live monitoring. Unsatisfied by the Board’s assurances, scores of aspirants held street protests in Jammu. Vinkal Sharma, an activist, said, “We demand postponement of the SI examination till the Board maintains transparency.” The J&K Students Association (JKSA) alleged that Mr. Sharma and over a dozen other protesters were detained by the police. “The detentions are deeply unfortunate and unjustified. It is an attempt to suppress legitimate democratic dissent. All detained students and aspirants should be released,” said the Association. Former Member of Parliament Aga Syed Ruhullah, in a post on X, said, “Enough of this blame game between the two power centres. They must stop passing responsibility and start acting. Postpone the November 29 JKPSI examination and constitute an independent SIT to probe the alleged JKSSB FAA irregularities. They are demanding justice, transparency and accountability. Their future cannot be held hostage to administrative failures.”

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: On November 15, the J&K Police busted four “cheating modules” in Jammu during the Board’s examination for the FAA posts. Nearly 1.62 lakh aspirants had appeared for around 600 posts across J&K. The Board has faced more than three major allegations of scams during recruitment examinations in the past six years.

🏛️ Political, National & Polity Paragraph #11 of 30 (27 NOV)

📰 Jammu and Kashmir’s selection board’s official X handle ‘suspended’ amid anti-board protests over cheating case

📌 Published: 27 Nov 2026, 02:22:42 AM
🎙️ Desi Hinglish Voice Educator • 🚂 Live Train Line Highlight & Screen Lock

1. Core Context & Background: Official sources said the official handle of the Board on X was suspended on November 25, 2026, apparently due to large-scale reporting by protesting netizens online

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: The official X handle of the J&K Service Selection Board (JKSSB) was reportedly suspended on Thursday (November 26, 2026), as protests against the recruitment board continued in the wake of the recent case of cheating during the Finance Accounts Assistant (FAA) examination in Jammu. Meanwhile, activists and aspirants, who were seeking postponement of the Sub-Inspector examination, were allegedly detained in Jammu. Official sources said the official handle of the Board on X was suspended on Wednesday (November 25), apparently due to large-scale reporting by protesting netizens online. The JKSSB has not issued any statement on the suspension of its X handle. It had around 129.1K followers. Meanwhile, several aspirants held protests in Jammu against the Board and demanded postponement of the upcoming Police Sub-Inspector (PSI) examination scheduled for November 29. Meanwhile, the Board said it put in place fresh measures to check cheating. It has asked the Deputy Commissioners to appoint invigilation staff through a randomisation process, drawing from a pool of staff already identified. “Exam centres will be allotted to candidates at random, but admit cards will now be available for download only three days before the exam instead of seven,” it said. The magistrates have been tasked to supervise the frisking of candidates and exam staff. All staff deployed at a centre, including service providers, will have to hand in their mobile phones and other gadgets, which will be kept locked in the centre’s control room until the exam ends, it added. The Board also increased jammers at exam centres and pressed CCTV for live monitoring. Unsatisfied by the Board’s assurances, scores of aspirants held street protests in Jammu. Vinkal Sharma, an activist, said, “We demand postponement of the SI examination till the Board maintains transparency.” The J&K Students Association (JKSA) alleged that Mr. Sharma and over a dozen other protesters were detained by the police. “The detentions are deeply unfortunate and unjustified. It is an attempt to suppress legitimate democratic dissent. All detained students and aspirants should be released,” said the Association. Former Member of Parliament Aga Syed Ruhullah, in a post on X, said, “Enough of this blame game between the two power centres. They must stop passing responsibility and start acting. Postpone the November 29 JKPSI examination and constitute an independent SIT to probe the alleged JKSSB FAA irregularities. They are demanding justice, transparency and accountability. Their future cannot be held hostage to administrative failures.”

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: On November 15, the J&K Police busted four “cheating modules” in Jammu during the Board’s examination for the FAA posts. Nearly 1.62 lakh aspirants had appeared for around 600 posts across J&K. The Board has faced more than three major allegations of scams during recruitment examinations in the past six years.

✓ Syn: Responsibility, Answerability, Liability  |  ✖ Ant: Immunity, Exemption, Irresponsibility

ज़िम्मेदारी — इस अनुच्छेद में 'Responsibility' का प्रयोग एक महत्वपूर्ण प्रशासनिक और विश्लेषणात्मक अर्थ में किया गया है।

articles.keyPoints:
• 1. Core Context & Background: Official sources said the official handle of the Board on X was suspended on November 25, 2026, apparently due to large-scale reporting by protesting netizens online
• 2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: The official X handle of the J&K Service Selection Board (JKSSB) was reportedly suspended on Thursday (November 26, 2026), as protests against the recruitment board continued in the wake of the recent case of cheating during the Finance Accounts Assistant (FAA) examination in Jammu. Meanwhile, activists and aspirants, who were seeking postponement of the Sub-Inspector examination, were allegedly detained in Jammu. Official sources said the official handle of the Board on X was suspended on Wednesday (November 25), apparently due to large-scale reporting by protesting netizens online. The JKSSB has not issued any statement on the suspension of its X handle. It had around 129.1K followers. Meanwhile, several aspirants held protests in Jammu against the Board and demanded postponement of the upcoming Police Sub-Inspector (PSI) examination scheduled for November 29. Meanwhile, the Board said it put in place fresh measures to check cheating. It has asked the Deputy Commissioners to appoint invigilation staff through a randomisation process, drawing from a pool of staff already identified. “Exam centres will be allotted to candidates at random, but admit cards will now be available for download only three days before the exam instead of seven,” it said. The magistrates have been tasked to supervise the frisking of candidates and exam staff. All staff deployed at a centre, including service providers, will have to hand in their mobile phones and other gadgets, which will be kept locked in the centre’s control room until the exam ends, it added. The Board also increased jammers at exam centres and pressed CCTV for live monitoring. Unsatisfied by the Board’s assurances, scores of aspirants held street protests in Jammu. Vinkal Sharma, an activist, said, “We demand postponement of the SI examination till the Board maintains transparency.” The J&K Students Association (JKSA) alleged that Mr. Sharma and over a dozen other protesters were detained by the police. “The detentions are deeply unfortunate and unjustified. It is an attempt to suppress legitimate democratic dissent. All detained students and aspirants should be released,” said the Association. Former Member of Parliament Aga Syed Ruhullah, in a post on X, said, “Enough of this blame game between the two power centres. They must stop passing responsibility and start acting. Postpone the November 29 JKPSI examination and constitute an independent SIT to probe the alleged JKSSB FAA irregularities. They are demanding justice, transparency and accountability. Their future cannot be held hostage to administrative failures.”
• 3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: On November 15, the J&K Police busted four “cheating modules” in Jammu during the Board’s examination for the FAA posts. Nearly 1.62 lakh aspirants had appeared for around 600 posts across J&K. The Board has faced more than three major allegations of scams during recruitment examinations in the past six years.

Patil held discussions with four Japanese companies on Thursday, the fourth day of his visit to Japan, focusing on their existing operations in Karnataka and expansion plans. According to a release, during a meeting with Seiren Co. At a meeting with the leadership of Enomoto Co. articles.title: Strobe Talbott, former Time magazine reporter and Deputy Secretary of State, has died
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: 1. Core Context & Background: While at the British university, after interning for Time in Moscow, the magazine asked Talbott to help translate the leaked memoirs of Nikita Khrushchev

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: Strobe Talbott, a former Time magazine reporter who later served as Deputy Secretary of State under President Bill Clinton and then headed the Brookings Institution, died Thursday (November 26, 2026). He was 80. His son, Devin Talbott, confirmed he passed away peacefully after a long illness in his East Hampton, New York, home. The elder Talbott was educated at Yale and Oxford, where he bunked with Mr. Clinton. While at the British university, after interning for Time in Moscow, the magazine asked Talbott to help translate the leaked memoirs of Nikita Khrushchev, the former first secretary of the Communist Party of the Soviet Union, who was ousted in 1964. Talbott did, and it gave him some notoriety as a young man and a job at the magazine. After 21 years at Time , where he focused on Soviet-American relations and held positions including Washington bureau chief and a foreign-affairs columnist, according to his US State Department biography, he received a call from the newly elected Clinton. Then-Prime Minister P.V. Narasimha Rao in conversation with visiting then-U.S. Deputy Secretary of State Strobe Talbot, in New Delhi on April 08, 1994. | Photo Credit: UNI Talbott joined the U.S. State Department in 1994, swiftly becoming Deputy Secretary of State. In that role, he was the architect of the Clinton administration's approach to Russia and other formerly Soviet countries and conducted negotiations between the US and India after the latter's nuclear tests in 1998. Afterward, he served as the president of Brookings from 2002 to 2017. In that time, he also chaired the U.S. State Department's Foreign Affairs Policy Board. Talbott also authored over a dozen books. His last book was titled “Our Founders' Warning: The Age of Reason Meets the Age of Trump,” which was published in 2020.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: He was born in Dayton, Ohio, in 1946, and is survived by two sons, Devin and Adrian; stepdaughter Rebecca Ascher-Walsh; siblings Kirk, Marjo and Page Talbott; and eight grandchildren, according to the New York Times.

🌐 International & Geopolitics Paragraph #24 of 30 (27 NOV)

📰 Strobe Talbott, former Time magazine reporter and Deputy Secretary of State, has died

📌 Published: 27 Nov 2026, 10:28:12 AM
🎙️ Desi Hinglish Voice Educator • 🚂 Live Train Line Highlight & Screen Lock

1. Core Context & Background: While at the British university, after interning for Time in Moscow, the magazine asked Talbott to help translate the leaked memoirs of Nikita Khrushchev

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: Strobe Talbott, a former Time magazine reporter who later served as Deputy Secretary of State under President Bill Clinton and then headed the Brookings Institution, died Thursday (November 26, 2026). He was 80. His son, Devin Talbott, confirmed he passed away peacefully after a long illness in his East Hampton, New York, home. The elder Talbott was educated at Yale and Oxford, where he bunked with Mr. Clinton. While at the British university, after interning for Time in Moscow, the magazine asked Talbott to help translate the leaked memoirs of Nikita Khrushchev, the former first secretary of the Communist Party of the Soviet Union, who was ousted in 1964. Talbott did, and it gave him some notoriety as a young man and a job at the magazine. After 21 years at Time , where he focused on Soviet-American relations and held positions including Washington bureau chief and a foreign-affairs columnist, according to his US State Department biography, he received a call from the newly elected Clinton. Then-Prime Minister P.V. Narasimha Rao in conversation with visiting then-U.S. Deputy Secretary of State Strobe Talbot, in New Delhi on April 08, 1994. | Photo Credit: UNI Talbott joined the U.S. State Department in 1994, swiftly becoming Deputy Secretary of State. In that role, he was the architect of the Clinton administration's approach to Russia and other formerly Soviet countries and conducted negotiations between the US and India after the latter's nuclear tests in 1998. Afterward, he served as the president of Brookings from 2002 to 2017. In that time, he also chaired the U.S. State Department's Foreign Affairs Policy Board. Talbott also authored over a dozen books. His last book was titled “Our Founders' Warning: The Age of Reason Meets the Age of Trump,” which was published in 2020.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: He was born in Dayton, Ohio, in 1946, and is survived by two sons, Devin and Adrian; stepdaughter Rebecca Ascher-Walsh; siblings Kirk, Marjo and Page Talbott; and eight grandchildren, according to the New York Times.

articles.title: TG SAFE discards decomposed fish at Hyderabad markets
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: 1. Core Context & Background: Officials also found establishments operating without a licence and under unhygienic conditions

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: The Telangana Standards Authority for Food and Essential Drugs (TG SAFE) Food Wing discarded around 420 kg of spoiled and decomposed fish during inspections at Begum Bazaar and Ramnagar fish markets in Hyderabad on Friday (November 27, 2026). Several traders were also issued notices for operating without mandatory food safety licences. At Begum Bazaar, officials inspected GNB Sri Srinivasa Fish Merchant and conducted spot tests for formalin and nitrates. Based on their observations and the opinion of a veterinary officer, they discarded 70 kg of catla fish and directed the trader to obtain the required food business registration. Food wing of Telangana Standards Authority for Food and Essential Drugs (TG SAFE) conducted spot tests for formalin and nitrates during inspections at fish markets and outlets in Hyderabad on Friday (November 27, 2026) | Photo Credit: BY ARRANGEMENT At Ramnagar fish market in Musheerabad, teams inspected several establishments, including Hari Fish Company, Arjun Fish Mart, Balakrishna Fish Mart, CNR Enterprises and JDB Fish Merchant. Around 150 kg of fish, valued at ₹15,000, was discarded, and notices were issued to the establishments for operating without FSSAI licences. Inspections were also conducted at Laxmi Narayana Wholesale Fish Shop, SKK Fish Merchants, KLM Fish Merchants, SVR Wholesale Fish Merchant, GBK Fish and Binsons Fishery. Traders were directed to obtain the required food licences. Officials discarded 70 kg of decomposed fish worth ₹5,400 at SKK and KLM Fish Merchants, 35 kg of decomposed Tilapia worth ₹1,400 at SVR Wholesale Fish Merchant, and 30 kg of decomposed fish worth ₹3,000 at GBK Fish. At Binsons Fishery, 65 kg of spoiled fish valued at ₹8,450 was discarded. Officials also found the establishment operating without a licence and under unhygienic conditions. The inspections were conducted by TG SAFE Food Wing personnel along with veterinary officers and police personnel. Fish outlets and markets in Begum Bazaar and Ramnagar were inspected by the food wing of Telangana Standards Authority for Food and Essential Drugs (TG SAFE) on Friday (November 27, 2026) | Photo Credit: BY ARRANGEMENT Hyderabad Police seize 90 tonnes of illegal chicken waste intended for fish feed
3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: ₹47-crore wholesale fish market planned in Hyderabad under ₹353-crore fisheries push

🏛️ Political, National & Polity Paragraph #7 of 30 (27 NOV)

📰 TG SAFE discards decomposed fish at Hyderabad markets

📌 Published: 27 Nov 2026, 11:52:40 AM
🎙️ Desi Hinglish Voice Educator • 🚂 Live Train Line Highlight & Screen Lock

1. Core Context & Background: Officials also found establishments operating without a licence and under unhygienic conditions

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: The Telangana Standards Authority for Food and Essential Drugs (TG SAFE) Food Wing discarded around 420 kg of spoiled and decomposed fish during inspections at Begum Bazaar and Ramnagar fish markets in Hyderabad on Friday (November 27, 2026). Several traders were also issued notices for operating without mandatory food safety licences. At Begum Bazaar, officials inspected GNB Sri Srinivasa Fish Merchant and conducted spot tests for formalin and nitrates. Based on their observations and the opinion of a veterinary officer, they discarded 70 kg of catla fish and directed the trader to obtain the required food business registration. Food wing of Telangana Standards Authority for Food and Essential Drugs (TG SAFE) conducted spot tests for formalin and nitrates during inspections at fish markets and outlets in Hyderabad on Friday (November 27, 2026) | Photo Credit: BY ARRANGEMENT At Ramnagar fish market in Musheerabad, teams inspected several establishments, including Hari Fish Company, Arjun Fish Mart, Balakrishna Fish Mart, CNR Enterprises and JDB Fish Merchant. Around 150 kg of fish, valued at ₹15,000, was discarded, and notices were issued to the establishments for operating without FSSAI licences. Inspections were also conducted at Laxmi Narayana Wholesale Fish Shop, SKK Fish Merchants, KLM Fish Merchants, SVR Wholesale Fish Merchant, GBK Fish and Binsons Fishery. Traders were directed to obtain the required food licences. Officials discarded 70 kg of decomposed fish worth ₹5,400 at SKK and KLM Fish Merchants, 35 kg of decomposed Tilapia worth ₹1,400 at SVR Wholesale Fish Merchant, and 30 kg of decomposed fish worth ₹3,000 at GBK Fish. At Binsons Fishery, 65 kg of spoiled fish valued at ₹8,450 was discarded. Officials also found the establishment operating without a licence and under unhygienic conditions. The inspections were conducted by TG SAFE Food Wing personnel along with veterinary officers and police personnel. Fish outlets and markets in Begum Bazaar and Ramnagar were inspected by the food wing of Telangana Standards Authority for Food and Essential Drugs (TG SAFE) on Friday (November 27, 2026) | Photo Credit: BY ARRANGEMENT Hyderabad Police seize 90 tonnes of illegal chicken waste intended for fish feed

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: ₹47-crore wholesale fish market planned in Hyderabad under ₹353-crore fisheries push

महत्वपूर्ण विश्लेषणात्मक शब्द — इस लेख में 'Registration' मुख्य प्रभाव और नीतिगत स्थिति को स्पष्ट करता है।
✓ Syn: Significant, Substantial, Strategic  |  ✖ Ant: Insignificant, Negligible, Trivial
Arrangement (Adjective)
महत्वपूर्ण विश्लेषणात्मक शब्द — इस लेख में 'Arrangement' मुख्य प्रभाव और नीतिगत स्थिति को स्पष्ट करता है।
✓ Syn: Comprehensive, Influential, Decisive  |  ✖ Ant: Superficial, Ineffective, Fragile
Unhygienic (Adjective)
महत्वपूर्ण विश्लेषणात्मक शब्द — इस लेख में 'Unhygienic' मुख्य प्रभाव और नीतिगत स्थिति को स्पष्ट करता है।

Q1. Based on a critical reading of the above 🏛️ Political, National & Polity passage on "TG SAFE discards decomposed fish at Hyderabad markets", which of the following statements accurately reflects the central analytical observation of the text?
A. Officials also found establishments operating without a licence and under unhygienic conditions.
B. Contrary to the passage, the issue of 'TG SAFE discards decomposed fish at Hyderabad ma' requires zero institutional or regulatory intervention at any level.

D. The author contends that 'TG SAFE discards decomposed fish at Hyderabad' has no bearing on public governance, economy, or citizen welfare.

✅ Correct Answer: Option (B) — Sahi Jawab Option (B) hai. articles.title: Kanchi pontiff opens hall at Thyagaraja Mandapam in Tirupati, urges protection of heritage
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: 1. Core Context & Background: Kanchi pontiff Shankara Vijayendra Saraswathi calls on the present generation to protect and preserve ancient heritage, values and culture

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: Kanchi Kamakoti Peetham’s 70th pontiff Shankara Vijayendra Saraswathi has called on the present generation to protect and preserve the ancient heritage, values and culture that define Hindu society. He described culture as the cornerstone of the temple ecosystem. The seer formally inaugurated the multi-purpose function hall of the Sri Thyagaraja Swamy Cultural Trust in Tirupati on Thursday (November 26, 2026). Thyagaraja Mandapam, located in the heart of the city, has remained the cultural nerve centre of Tirupati for almost a century, with classical music concerts held there every year. With the passage of time, a multi-purpose hall was built at the same venue to carry on the legacy of holding music concerts, while meeting the needs of modern times. The seer hailed fine arts such as music and dance as a way of spreading devotion. The trust’s executive chairman K.V. Mohan Sundaram, secretary Kanchi Raghuramaiah and the Mutt’s disciples, musicians and common devotees took part. Later, the Sri Kanchi Veda Vedantha Sastra Sabha conducted its convocation ( ‘Deekshanta Samarohaha’ ) for scholars who passed rigorous tests spread across 12 to 14 semesters. At the annual event, started by Anjaneya Sastri in 1999, 125 awards were presented to scholars who excelled in Nyaya, Vyakarana, Mimamsa, Vedanta, Advaita Siddhi Ratnakara, Patanjali Mahabhashya, Bhamathi Prasthanam and Veda Bhashya.
3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: Fifteen scholars received awards after clearing a demanding examination popularly known as the ‘Tenali Pariksha’ .

🏛️ Political, National & Polity Paragraph #9 of 30 (27 NOV)

📰 Kanchi pontiff opens hall at Thyagaraja Mandapam in Tirupati, urges protection of heritage

📌 Published: 27 Nov 2026, 11:48:33 AM
🎙️ Desi Hinglish Voice Educator • 🚂 Live Train Line Highlight & Screen Lock

1. Core Context & Background: Kanchi pontiff Shankara Vijayendra Saraswathi calls on the present generation to protect and preserve ancient heritage, values and culture

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: Kanchi Kamakoti Peetham’s 70th pontiff Shankara Vijayendra Saraswathi has called on the present generation to protect and preserve the ancient heritage, values and culture that define Hindu society. He described culture as the cornerstone of the temple ecosystem. The seer formally inaugurated the multi-purpose function hall of the Sri Thyagaraja Swamy Cultural Trust in Tirupati on Thursday (November 26, 2026). Thyagaraja Mandapam, located in the heart of the city, has remained the cultural nerve centre of Tirupati for almost a century, with classical music concerts held there every year. With the passage of time, a multi-purpose hall was built at the same venue to carry on the legacy of holding music concerts, while meeting the needs of modern times. The seer hailed fine arts such as music and dance as a way of spreading devotion. The trust’s executive chairman K.V. Mohan Sundaram, secretary Kanchi Raghuramaiah and the Mutt’s disciples, musicians and common devotees took part. Later, the Sri Kanchi Veda Vedantha Sastra Sabha conducted its convocation ( ‘Deekshanta Samarohaha’ ) for scholars who passed rigorous tests spread across 12 to 14 semesters. At the annual event, started by Anjaneya Sastri in 1999, 125 awards were presented to scholars who excelled in Nyaya, Vyakarana, Mimamsa, Vedanta, Advaita Siddhi Ratnakara, Patanjali Mahabhashya, Bhamathi Prasthanam and Veda Bhashya.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: Fifteen scholars received awards after clearing a demanding examination popularly known as the ‘Tenali Pariksha’ .

महत्वपूर्ण विश्लेषणात्मक शब्द — इस लेख में 'Convocation' मुख्य प्रभाव और नीतिगत स्थिति को स्पष्ट करता है।

Generation (Noun)
महत्वपूर्ण विश्लेषणात्मक शब्द — इस लेख में 'Generation' मुख्य प्रभाव और नीतिगत स्थिति को स्पष्ट करता है।
✓ Syn: Significant, Substantial, Strategic  |  ✖ Ant: Insignificant, Negligible, Trivial
Classical (Adjective)
महत्वपूर्ण विश्लेषणात्मक शब्द — इस लेख में 'Classical' मुख्य प्रभाव और नीतिगत स्थिति को स्पष्ट करता है।

articles.title: 100% placement record drives demand for GTTC courses in Karnataka, intake increases to 6,000
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: 1. Core Context & Background: Nearly 10,000 applications received this academic year; government plans six-month aerospace courses and foreign language training to meet industry requirements

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: Amid growing demand from students and parents, the Karnataka government has increased the student intake at Government Tool Room and Training Centres (GTTCs) across the State to 6,000 for the current academic year, up from the earlier capacity of 5,000. The increase comes as the technical training institutes witness a surge in applications, driven largely by their industry-oriented curriculum and reported 100% placement record. Read | Five Government Tool Room and Training Centre students selected by Germany’s Rheinbahn AG There are 33 GTTCs across Karnataka. The total intake capacity at these institutes stood at 2,500 during the 2023-24 academic year. Recognising the growing demand and the need to create employment opportunities for more students, the government increased the intake to 5,000 for the 2025-26 academic year. An additional 1,000 seats have now been added for the current academic year, according to officials. Nearly 10,000 applications were received this year, prompting the government to expand the intake capacity. Admissions have been completed through a centralised counselling process conducted by the Karnataka Examinations Authority (KEA). “GTTC is the only institute where 100% placement is achieved. Consequently, there has been immense demand from students, with nearly 10,000 applications received this year. Therefore, increasing the intake capacity became necessary, and the intake has been raised to 6,000. The seats have been filled through a centralised counselling process conducted by the KEA,” said Sharan Prakash Patil, Minister for Medical Education and Skill Development, Entrepreneurship and Livelihood. The three-year diploma programmes offered by GTTCs, along with their short-term courses, focus on practical training to prepare students for industry requirements. The curriculum comprises 60% hands-on training and 40% theoretical instruction, with students spending a significant part of their course working directly on machines. This is followed by a one-year industrial internship, giving students practical exposure and the technical skills required by the manufacturing sector. The government has also introduced a ‘Train While Learning’ initiative, under which students in their final semester receive soft-skills training from multinational companies.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: Along with increasing the intake, the government is planning to strengthen infrastructure and upgrade equipment across the 33 institutes to accommodate more students.

🏛️ Political, National & Polity Paragraph #11 of 30 (27 NOV)

📰 100% placement record drives demand for GTTC courses in Karnataka, intake increases to 6,000

📌 Published: 27 Nov 2026, 11:46:41 AM
🎙️ Desi Hinglish Voice Educator • 🚂 Live Train Line Highlight & Screen Lock

1. Core Context & Background: Nearly 10,000 applications received this academic year; government plans six-month aerospace courses and foreign language training to meet industry requirements

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: Amid growing demand from students and parents, the Karnataka government has increased the student intake at Government Tool Room and Training Centres (GTTCs) across the State to 6,000 for the current academic year, up from the earlier capacity of 5,000. The increase comes as the technical training institutes witness a surge in applications, driven largely by their industry-oriented curriculum and reported 100% placement record. Read | Five Government Tool Room and Training Centre students selected by Germany’s Rheinbahn AG There are 33 GTTCs across Karnataka. The total intake capacity at these institutes stood at 2,500 during the 2023-24 academic year. Recognising the growing demand and the need to create employment opportunities for more students, the government increased the intake to 5,000 for the 2025-26 academic year. An additional 1,000 seats have now been added for the current academic year, according to officials. Nearly 10,000 applications were received this year, prompting the government to expand the intake capacity. Admissions have been completed through a centralised counselling process conducted by the Karnataka Examinations Authority (KEA). “GTTC is the only institute where 100% placement is achieved. Consequently, there has been immense demand from students, with nearly 10,000 applications received this year. Therefore, increasing the intake capacity became necessary, and the intake has been raised to 6,000. The seats have been filled through a centralised counselling process conducted by the KEA,” said Sharan Prakash Patil, Minister for Medical Education and Skill Development, Entrepreneurship and Livelihood. The three-year diploma programmes offered by GTTCs, along with their short-term courses, focus on practical training to prepare students for industry requirements. The curriculum comprises 60% hands-on training and 40% theoretical instruction, with students spending a significant part of their course working directly on machines. This is followed by a one-year industrial internship, giving students practical exposure and the technical skills required by the manufacturing sector. The government has also introduced a ‘Train While Learning’ initiative, under which students in their final semester receive soft-skills training from multinational companies.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: Along with increasing the intake, the government is planning to strengthen infrastructure and upgrade equipment across the 33 institutes to accommodate more students.

संस्थागत — देश की संवैधानिक या सरकारी संस्थाओं के नियमों और ढांचे से जुड़ा हुआ।
✓ Syn: Systemic, Organizational, Constitutional  |  ✖ Ant: Individual, Informal, Unorganized

महत्वपूर्ण विश्लेषणात्मक शब्द — इस लेख में 'Multinational' मुख्य प्रभाव और नीतिगत स्थिति को स्पष्ट करता है।
✓ Syn: Comprehensive, Influential, Decisive  |  ✖ Ant: Superficial, Ineffective, Fragile
Development (Adjective)
महत्वपूर्ण विश्लेषणात्मक शब्द — इस लेख में 'Development' मुख्य प्रभाव और नीतिगत स्थिति को स्पष्ट करता है।
✓ Syn: Comprehensive, Influential, Decisive  |  ✖ Ant: Superficial, Ineffective, Fragile
Theoretical (Adjective)
सैद्धांतिक — इस अनुच्छेद में 'Theoretical' का प्रयोग एक महत्वपूर्ण प्रशासनिक और विश्लेषणात्मक अर्थ में किया गया है।
✓ Syn: Comprehensive, Influential, Decisive  |  ✖ Ant: Superficial, Ineffective, Fragile
🧠 2 ANALYTICAL EXAM QUESTIONS BASED ON THIS EDITORIAL:
Q1. Based on a critical reading of the above 🏛️ Political, National & Polity passage on "100% placement record drives demand for GTTC courses in Karnataka, intake increases to 6,000", which of the following statements accurately reflects the central analytical observation of the text?
A. Nearly 10,000 applications received this academic year; government plans six-month aerospace courses and foreign language training to meet industry...
B. Contrary to the passage, the issue of '100% placement record drives demand for GTTC cou' requires zero institutional or regulatory intervention at any level.
C. The passage argues that all empirical data and statutory mechanisms related to '100% placement record drives demand for GTTC ' should be permanently discontinued.
D. The author contends that '100% placement record drives demand for GTTC ' has no bearing on public governance, economy, or citizen welfare.
✅ Correct Answer: Option (A) — Sahi Jawab Option (A) hai. Is passage ki mukhya line saaf batati hai: "Nearly 10,000 applications received this academic year; government plans six-month aerospace courses and foreign language training to meet industry..." (Hinglish Arth: इस शैक्षणिक वर्ष में लगभग 10,000 आवेदन प्राप्त हुए; सरकार उद्योग की आवश्यकताओं को पूरा करने के लिए छह महीने के एयरोस्पेस पाठ्यक्रम और विदेशी भाषा प्रशिक्षण की योजना बना रही है)
Q2. Which of the following key analytical points or conclusions is explicitly highlighted by the author in the passage regarding "100% placement record drives demand for GTTC courses in Karnataka, intake increases to 6,000"?
A. Advocating complete policy paralysis and ignoring ground-level implementation challenges.
B. Along with increasing the intake, the government is planning to strengthen infrastructure and upgrade equipment across the 33 institutes to...
C. Dismissing constitutional accountability and relying solely on unverified short-term measures.
D. Recommending the immediate suspension of all regulatory and scientific assessments mentioned in the text.
✅ Correct Answer: Option (B) — Sahi Jawab Option (B) hai. Lekhak ne passage ke vishleshan mein is baat par zor diya hai: "Along with increasing the intake, the government is planning to strengthen infrastructure and upgrade equipment across the 33 institutes to..." (Hinglish Arth: प्रवेश बढ़ाने के साथ-साथ, सरकार अधिक छात्रों को समायोजित करने के लिए 33 संस्थानों में बुनियादी ढांचे को मजबूत करने और उपकरणों को उन्नत करने की योजना बना रही है।)

articles.title: Two arrested with charas worth ₹12.20 crore at Lokmanya Tilak Terminus in Mumbai
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: 1. Core Context & Background: Anti-Narcotics Cell dispatches team to Uttar Pradesh to investigate suspected links in the drug supply network

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: The Worli unit of the Mumbai Crime Branch’s Anti-Narcotics Cell (ANC) arrested two persons after allegedly recovering 12.2 kg of charas worth ₹12.20 crore from their possession at Lokmanya Tilak Terminus (LTT) during an operation conducted on the intervening night of November 24 and 25. A case was registered on November 25 under Sections 8(c), 20(c) and 29 of the Narcotic Drugs and Psychotropic Substances (NDPS) Act, 1985. According to the police, an ANC team was conducting an operation to identify individuals involved in the sale, purchase, supply and storage of narcotic substances across Mumbai when officers noticed two persons moving suspiciously at the railway terminus. The officers intercepted the duo and allegedly recovered 12.2 kg of charas, with an estimated market value of ₹12.20 crore. Both accused were subsequently arrested. During the investigation, the accused reportedly disclosed information about other suspected links in the drug supply network, following which a police team was dispatched to Uttar Pradesh for further investigation.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: The operation was carried out under the supervision of Deputy Commissioner of Police (ANC) Pournima Chougule-Shringi and led by Senior Police Inspector Santosh Salunkhe, along with Police Inspector Digambar Patil, Police Sub-Inspector Mukund Jadhav and their team.

🏛️ Political, National & Polity Paragraph #12 of 30 (27 NOV)

📰 Two arrested with charas worth ₹12.20 crore at Lokmanya Tilak Terminus in Mumbai

📌 Published: 27 Nov 2026, 11:45:50 AM
🎙️ Desi Hinglish Voice Educator • 🚂 Live Train Line Highlight & Screen Lock

1. Core Context & Background: Anti-Narcotics Cell dispatches team to Uttar Pradesh to investigate suspected links in the drug supply network

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: The Worli unit of the Mumbai Crime Branch’s Anti-Narcotics Cell (ANC) arrested two persons after allegedly recovering 12.2 kg of charas worth ₹12.20 crore from their possession at Lokmanya Tilak Terminus (LTT) during an operation conducted on the intervening night of November 24 and 25. A case was registered on November 25 under Sections 8(c), 20(c) and 29 of the Narcotic Drugs and Psychotropic Substances (NDPS) Act, 1985. According to the police, an ANC team was conducting an operation to identify individuals involved in the sale, purchase, supply and storage of narcotic substances across Mumbai when officers noticed two persons moving suspiciously at the railway terminus. The officers intercepted the duo and allegedly recovered 12.2 kg of charas, with an estimated market value of ₹12.20 crore. Both accused were subsequently arrested. During the investigation, the accused reportedly disclosed information about other suspected links in the drug supply network, following which a police team was dispatched to Uttar Pradesh for further investigation.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: The operation was carried out under the supervision of Deputy Commissioner of Police (ANC) Pournima Chougule-Shringi and led by Senior Police Inspector Santosh Salunkhe, along with Police Inspector Digambar Patil, Police Sub-Inspector Mukund Jadhav and their team.

articles.title: Costa Rica bars entry to UN rapporteur over ‘links to terrorist acts’
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: 1. Core Context & Background: Francesca Albanese arrived at the airport serving the capital, San Jose, to receive an honorary degree from the University of Costa Rica, a public university

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: Costa Rica's government said on Thursday (November 26, 2026) it had denied entry to UN rapporteur Francesca Albanese, who has accused Israel of genocide, because she was the subject of an "international alert over links to terrorist acts." Ms. Albanese, the UN special rapporteur on the Palestinian territories, arrived on Thursday (November 26) at the airport serving the capital, San Jose, to receive an honorary degree from the University of Costa Rica, a public university. Ms. Albanese "is the subject of an international alert over links to terrorist acts," Omer Badilla, director general of Costa Rica's immigration authority, which falls under the interior ministry, said in a video posted on social media. "I hope this clears up any doubts and makes clear the threat this woman poses to national security," he added. The rector's office at the institution, the country's most important and prestigious university, said in a statement that immigration authorities were "blocking" Ms. Albanese's entry and asked the government to explain the decision. The government of Costa Rican President Laura Fernández is a close ally of U.S. President Donald Trump and has pursued closer trade ties with Israel since she took office in May. Last December, Ms. Albanese criticised a free trade agreement between Costa Rica and Israel and called for its ratification to be put on hold, prompting a rebuke from the government, which accused her of interfering in domestic affairs. The United States, Israel's main ally, imposed sanctions on Ms. Albanese after she criticised Washington's policy on Gaza. "You see the face of empire the day you touch a nerve or cross its boundaries," Ms. Albanese wrote from the airport.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: The university said it was awarding the honorary doctorate, which it grants annually to a prominent figure, in recognition of her "solid academic background, experience, publications and work exposing wrongdoing."

🌐 International & Geopolitics Paragraph #19 of 30 (27 NOV)

📰 Costa Rica bars entry to UN rapporteur over ‘links to terrorist acts’

📌 Published: 27 Nov 2026, 11:33:21 AM
🎙️ Desi Hinglish Voice Educator • 🚂 Live Train Line Highlight & Screen Lock

1. Core Context & Background: Francesca Albanese arrived at the airport serving the capital, San Jose, to receive an honorary degree from the University of Costa Rica, a public university

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: Costa Rica's government said on Thursday (November 26, 2026) it had denied entry to UN rapporteur Francesca Albanese, who has accused Israel of genocide, because she was the subject of an "international alert over links to terrorist acts." Ms. Albanese, the UN special rapporteur on the Palestinian territories, arrived on Thursday (November 26) at the airport serving the capital, San Jose, to receive an honorary degree from the University of Costa Rica, a public university. Ms. Albanese "is the subject of an international alert over links to terrorist acts," Omer Badilla, director general of Costa Rica's immigration authority, which falls under the interior ministry, said in a video posted on social media. "I hope this clears up any doubts and makes clear the threat this woman poses to national security," he added. The rector's office at the institution, the country's most important and prestigious university, said in a statement that immigration authorities were "blocking" Ms. Albanese's entry and asked the government to explain the decision. The government of Costa Rican President Laura Fernández is a close ally of U.S. President Donald Trump and has pursued closer trade ties with Israel since she took office in May. Last December, Ms. Albanese criticised a free trade agreement between Costa Rica and Israel and called for its ratification to be put on hold, prompting a rebuke from the government, which accused her of interfering in domestic affairs. The United States, Israel's main ally, imposed sanctions on Ms. Albanese after she criticised Washington's policy on Gaza. "You see the face of empire the day you touch a nerve or cross its boundaries," Ms. Albanese wrote from the airport.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: The university said it was awarding the honorary doctorate, which it grants annually to a prominent figure, in recognition of her "solid academic background, experience, publications and work exposing wrongdoing."

articles.title: Major storm batters U.S. on Thanksgiving holiday; 400 flights cancelled

fullParagraphs: 1. Core Context & Background: New York’s famed Macy’s parade was postponed for the first time in its 100-year history

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: A powerful storm disrupted Thanksgiving celebrations for millions of Americans on Thursday (November 26, 2026), as New York’s famed Macy’s parade was postponed for the first time in its 100-year history. Heavy rain and strong winds from the “Nor’easter” battered the central and eastern United States, creating treacherous travel conditions during one of the country’s busiest holiday periods. As families were gathering for traditional holiday feasts, more than 900,000 homes and businesses were without power, with Pennsylvania, Maryland and Virginia particularly hard hit, according to tracking website PowerOutage. At airports, nearly 400 flights were canceled and over 2,000 were delayed in the United States, mostly in the East, figures from FlightAware showed. New York’s famed parade, which sees brightly colored balloons travel through the heart of Manhattan, was pushed back to Saturday (November 28, 2026) due to what organizers said was an “abundance of caution.” Millions of people typically gather to catch a glimpse of the festivities. The only other time the parade was not held on Thanksgiving Thursday was when it was canceled for three years during World War II. Organizers would have been only too aware of the gusting winds that wrecked the parade back in 1997 when a careening 18-foot figure of the “Cat in the Hat” toppled a lamppost, knocking one bystander unconscious. “While we are heartbroken that our parade was postponed, the safety of our partners, the safety of our participants — and spectators — is and always will be our top priority,” said Macy’s parade executive producer Will Coss. While flooding was reported up and down the East Coast, impacts were also felt inland, with powerful gusts and inundated soil leading to trees tumbling over onto power lines and homes.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: Authorities in the Maryland suburbs of the US capital, worried about the impact of power outages on the water treatment network, asked nearly two million customers to conserve tap water consumption.

New York’s famed parade, which sees brightly colored balloons travel through the heart of Manhattan, was pushed back to Saturday (November 28, 2026) due to what organizers said was an “abundance of caution.” Millions of people typically gather to catch a glimpse of the festivities. The only other time the parade was not held on Thanksgiving Thursday was when it was canceled for three years during World War II. Organizers would have been only too aware of the gusting winds that wrecked the parade back in 1997 when a careening 18-foot figure of the “Cat in the Hat” toppled a lamppost, knocking one bystander unconscious. “While we are heartbroken that our parade was postponed, the safety of our partners, the safety of our participants — and spectators — is and always will be our top priority,” said Macy’s parade executive producer Will Coss. While flooding was reported up and down the East Coast, impacts were also felt inland, with powerful gusts and inundated soil leading to trees tumbling over onto power lines and homes.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: Authorities in the Maryland suburbs of the US capital, worried about the impact of power outages on the water treatment network, asked nearly two million customers to conserve tap water consumption.

articles.keyPoints:
• 1. Core Context & Background: New York’s famed Macy’s parade was postponed for the first time in its 100-year history
• 2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: A powerful storm disrupted Thanksgiving celebrations for millions of Americans on Thursday (November 26, 2026), as New York’s famed Macy’s parade was postponed for the first time in its 100-year history. Heavy rain and strong winds from the “Nor’easter” battered the central and eastern United States, creating treacherous travel conditions during one of the country’s busiest holiday periods. As families were gathering for traditional holiday feasts, more than 900,000 homes and businesses were without power, with Pennsylvania, Maryland and Virginia particularly hard hit, according to tracking website PowerOutage. At airports, nearly 400 flights were canceled and over 2,000 were delayed in the United States, mostly in the East, figures from FlightAware showed. New York’s famed parade, which sees brightly colored balloons travel through the heart of Manhattan, was pushed back to Saturday (November 28, 2026) due to what organizers said was an “abundance of caution.” Millions of people typically gather to catch a glimpse of the festivities. The only other time the parade was not held on Thanksgiving Thursday was when it was canceled for three years during World War II. Organizers would have been only too aware of the gusting winds that wrecked the parade back in 1997 when a careening 18-foot figure of the “Cat in the Hat” toppled a lamppost, knocking one bystander unconscious. “While we are heartbroken that our parade was postponed, the safety of our partners, the safety of our participants — and spectators — is and always will be our top priority,” said Macy’s parade executive producer Will Coss. While flooding was reported up and down the East Coast, impacts were also felt inland, with powerful gusts and inundated soil leading to trees tumbling over onto power lines and homes.
• 3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: Authorities in the Maryland suburbs of the US capital, worried about the impact of power outages on the water treatment network, asked nearly two million customers to conserve tap water consumption.

articles.title: Canada’s top court rules on Quebec secularism law in landmark case
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: 1. Core Context & Background: The law has been the subject of intense legal debate since it was first passed by Quebec's government in 2019

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: The Supreme Court rules on Friday (November 27, 2026) on one of Canada's most closely watched cases -- a Quebec law barring some provincial employees from wearing religious symbols. The law has been the subject of intense legal debate since it was first passed by Quebec's government in 2019. That is partly due to the implications for Quebec, a majority French-speaking province where the decades-long battle to enforce secularism is a core issue and where the Catholic Church once wielded enormous influence over public life. The case reflects a conflict playing out elsewhere in the world as strictly secular states such as that of France face pressure typical of the Anglo-Saxon world for people to be able to practice their religion freely, including wearing whatever symbols of it that they wish. The Quebec case is also seen as a major test of how far provinces can go in defying provisions of the federal constitution by invoking the so-called "notwithstanding clause." That clause, a quirk of Canada's legal system, effectively allows provincial governments to pass laws that may breach Canada's constitution, known as the Charter of Rights and Freedoms. Quebec pre-emptively invoked the "notwithstanding clause" when passing its secularism bill, anticipating it would be challenged over constitutional protections guaranteeing freedom of religion and expression. Conservative-led provinces have also invoked the clause to defend legislation relating to transgender youth. In 2023, Saskatchewan used the clause to pass a law requiring schools to obtain parental consent before changing the pronouns used for children under 16.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: Alberta has also invoked the clause in relation to laws banning transgender girls from participating in female sports and restricting hormone therapy for individuals under 16.

articles.keyPoints:
• 1. Core Context & Background: The law has been the subject of intense legal debate since it was first passed by Quebec's government in 2019
• 2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: The Supreme Court rules on Friday (November 27, 2026) on one of Canada's most closely watched cases -- a Quebec law barring some provincial employees from wearing religious symbols. The law has been the subject of intense legal debate since it was first passed by Quebec's government in 2019. That is partly due to the implications for Quebec, a majority French-speaking province where the decades-long battle to enforce secularism is a core issue and where the Catholic Church once wielded enormous influence over public life. The case reflects a conflict playing out elsewhere in the world as strictly secular states such as that of France face pressure typical of the Anglo-Saxon world for people to be able to practice their religion freely, including wearing whatever symbols of it that they wish. The Quebec case is also seen as a major test of how far provinces can go in defying provisions of the federal constitution by invoking the so-called "notwithstanding clause." That clause, a quirk of Canada's legal system, effectively allows provincial governments to pass laws that may breach Canada's constitution, known as the Charter of Rights and Freedoms. Quebec pre-emptively invoked the "notwithstanding clause" when passing its secularism bill, anticipating it would be challenged over constitutional protections guaranteeing freedom of religion and expression. Conservative-led provinces have also invoked the clause to defend legislation relating to transgender youth. In 2023, Saskatchewan used the clause to pass a law requiring schools to obtain parental consent before changing the pronouns used for children under 16.
• 3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: Alberta has also invoked the clause in relation to laws banning transgender girls from participating in female sports and restricting hormone therapy for individuals under 16.

fullParagraphs: 1. Core Context & Background: South Korea repatriated six North Koreans by sea on Friday (November 27, 2026) ​after their fishing boat was found drifting ‌off the peninsula’s east coast earlier ​this month, while a seventh ⁠chose to remain, Seoul’s Unification Ministry said.

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: The North Korean fishing boat crossed the maritime ‌border off the Korean Peninsula’s east coast under its own power ‌at 8:33 a.m. (2333 GMT on Thursday) ‌and ⁠was met by a North ⁠Korean vessel waiting to the north, the Ministry said. The boat, carrying seven people, was found ​drifting in international waters ‌near South Korea’s Ulleung Island on November 3 and subsequently towed by South Korean military and coast guard authorities. South ‌Korea decided to repatriate six ​of them after confirming their wish through a joint investigation with ⁠the United Nations Command, the Ministry said. The seventh expressed a wish to remain ‌in South Korea and will receive protection as a North Korean defector, according to the ministry. The Ministry said the government had closely coordinated with the UN Command on notifying the North ‌of the repatriation plan and also sent updates ​over an international maritime communications network. Pyongyang has severed all direct communication ⁠channels with the South.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: South Korea considers ⁠North Koreans to be its citizens and offers protection to defectors. ‌About 31,500 were registered as living in the South as of June, according ​to Unification Ministry data.

articles.title: Brazil’s Lula appoints private banker as Finance Minister
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: 1. Core Context & Background: Lula’s shock election win in October sent stock markets tumbling while the national currency, the real, weakened significantly

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: Brazilian President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva has appointed private banking executive Luiz Carlos Trabuco as Finance Minister for his next term, the presidency said on Thursday (November 26, 2026). Mr. Lula’s shock election win in October sent stock markets tumbling while the national currency, the real, weakened significantly. The appointment of Mr. Trabuco, chairman of the board of Bradesco bank, aims to reassure the business community in Latin America’s largest economy. “Luiz Carlos Trabuco has accepted President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva’s invitation to take the helm of the finance ministry,” the presidency stated, specifying that the banker agreed to take the job during an afternoon meeting with the Brazilian leader. Mr. Lula will begin his fourth non-consecutive term in office in January and has so far only named one minister for that mandate. Bradesco is one of Brazil’s largest private banks. Ahead of the official announcement, rumors circulating about Mr. Trabuco’s new job appeared to restore market confidence. The Sao Paulo Stock Exchange was up 6% at closing on Thursday (November 26, 2026).
3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: The national currency meanwhile regained strength after briefly crossing the symbolic threshold of six reais to the dollar on Monday.

🌐 International & Geopolitics Paragraph #23 of 30 (27 NOV)

📰 Brazil’s Lula appoints private banker as Finance Minister

📌 Published: 27 Nov 2026, 10:34:00 AM
🎙️ Desi Hinglish Voice Educator • 🚂 Live Train Line Highlight & Screen Lock

1. Core Context & Background: Lula’s shock election win in October sent stock markets tumbling while the national currency, the real, weakened significantly

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: Brazilian President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva has appointed private banking executive Luiz Carlos Trabuco as Finance Minister for his next term, the presidency said on Thursday (November 26, 2026). Mr. Lula’s shock election win in October sent stock markets tumbling while the national currency, the real, weakened significantly. The appointment of Mr. Trabuco, chairman of the board of Bradesco bank, aims to reassure the business community in Latin America’s largest economy. “Luiz Carlos Trabuco has accepted President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva’s invitation to take the helm of the finance ministry,” the presidency stated, specifying that the banker agreed to take the job during an afternoon meeting with the Brazilian leader. Mr. Lula will begin his fourth non-consecutive term in office in January and has so far only named one minister for that mandate. Bradesco is one of Brazil’s largest private banks. Ahead of the official announcement, rumors circulating about Mr. Trabuco’s new job appeared to restore market confidence. The Sao Paulo Stock Exchange was up 6% at closing on Thursday (November 26, 2026).

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: The national currency meanwhile regained strength after briefly crossing the symbolic threshold of six reais to the dollar on Monday.

D. The author contends that 'Brazil’s Lula appoints private banker as Fina' has no bearing on public governance, economy, or citizen welfare.
✅ Correct Answer: Option (A) — Sahi Jawab Option (A) hai. D. Recommending the immediate suspension of all regulatory and scientific assessments mentioned in the text.
✅ Correct Answer: Option (B) — Sahi Jawab Option (B) hai.
